title: Completed constant realization of finite complexes and their reductions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, and assume $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite for every $n$. Put $C=\varprojlim P_n$ and $J=IC$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X$ be a scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\widehat A_X=\varprojlim\underline{P_n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For a finite $C$-module $N$ put $c_X(N)=\varprojlim_n\underline{N/J^nN}$. The functor $c_X$ from finitely generated $C$-modules to sheaves of $\widehat A_X$-modules is exact and its values are adic lisse of finite type [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module]. For a bounded complex $Q$ of finite $C$-modules, write $c_X(Q)$ for its termwise realization. Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$c_X(Q)\otimes^L_{\widehat A_X}\underline{P_n}\simeq\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}$$
in the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], compatible with quotient transitions. For a scheme morphism $u:X\to T$, the same complex is a complex of $B=u^{-1}\widehat A_T$-modules via the projection-induced map $B\to\widehat A_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There are natural isomorphisms
$$c_X(Q)\otimes_B^L u^{-1}\underline{(P_n)_T}\simeq\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}_X.$$
These commute with all quotient reductions; no identification $u^{-1}\widehat A_T=\widehat A_X$ is asserted. Here derived tensors use K-flat resolutions as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

proof.text: Construct the scalar map constant(C) -> H by the cone whose components are constant evaluation C -> A/I^(n+1). Cauchy compatibility proves successor naturality; the limit universal property gives all its projections. Apply the module-level model theorem with this map. Quotient constant functors are additive.

Completion is Noetherian. A bounded finite complex has bounded-above finite homology. By the proved Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion its derived object is represented by a bounded-above finite-free complex. Projectivity of that complex lifts the derived isomorphism to an actual chain map (derived maps out of a bounded-above projective complex are represented by chain maps), and the localization criterion makes it a quasi-isomorphism.

Lift the finite source and target of any resolution to the abelian category of finitely generated modules. Its faithful exact inclusion reflects quasi-isomorphisms. Exactness of the finite realization, followed by exact scalar restriction, therefore preserves each resolution quasi-isomorphism. Construct the quotient-module tower explicitly: its transition maps are the actual ring-system maps, linear by the limit projection equations. Construct its universal derived tensor tower using the separately proved resolving-class construction. For a coefficient isomorphism apply the finite-free tensor calculation to that tower. Localize the realized resolution and invert that natural isomorphism, apply the derived tensor functor, then compose its K-flat counit with the tensor-calculation isomorphism. This is the required natural isomorphism of entire quotient diagrams.

For relative coefficients apply the already proved profinite coefficient inverse-image theorem to the actual tower of finite rings A/I^(n+1). Identify its constant tower with the original ofOpSequence ring system by identity components. Transport the canonical profinite comparison across the induced limit isomorphisms. It is an isomorphism and has exactly the required projections. Apply the preceding calculation to its scalar restriction. No preservation of arbitrary infinite limits is used.
